info.name: Restaurant Reservation System API - Assignment 2
info.description:
Full CRUD over three entities (Customer, RestaurantTable, Reservation) exposed as a Spring Boot REST API.

Run the folders top to bottom. The Setup folder stores ids and a future date in collection variables, so every later request works without editing anything by hand.

Base URL: http://localhost:8080

exec: // Always book 7 days ahead so the "no past bookings" rule never trips by accident.

item.name: 1. Setup and Customer CRUD
item.description: Entity 1 of 3. Run this folder first: it stores {{customerId}} and {{secondCustomerId}}.

request.description: BR-01. Saves the id into {{customerId}}.
A second customer, used later to prove one table cannot be double booked.
BR-02: two customers may not share an email address.
BR-09: blank name, malformed email and a phone that fails the 07xxxxxxxx pattern are all reported at once.
BR-03: one keyword searched across first name, last name, email and phone.
Any id that does not exist returns a 404 with a readable message.
BR-04. The uniqueness rule is re-checked on update.
Saves the id into {{tableId}}.
Status is optional on create and defaults to AVAILABLE. Saved as {{smallTableId}}.
Table numbers are unique across the restaurant.
Capacity must be between 1 and 20 seats.

item.name: READ - filter by status and capacity (200)

request.description: Finds every available table seating at least 4 guests.

item.name: UPDATE - move table to the garden (200)
3. Reservation CRUD and business rules
item.description: Entity 3 of 3, where most of the business logic lives.

item.name: CREATE - book table T1 for 4 guests (201)

request.description: The happy path. Saved as {{reservationId}}, status starts at PENDING.
Rule R-6. Each booking holds the table for 120 minutes, so 20:00 still falls inside the 19:00 slot.

item.name: CREATE - party larger than the table (422)

request.description: Rule R-4: a party of 8 cannot be seated at a 2-seat table.
Rule R-2.
Rule R-3: the restaurant takes bookings between 09:00 and 23:00.
Rule R-1.
BR-09: the table, date and time are required and party size must be at least 1.
The day sheet: every booking for one date, in time order.

item.name: UPDATE - change time and party size (200)

request.description: Every rule is re-checked on update, and the booking is excluded from its own overlap check.
Rule R-8: PENDING -> CONFIRMED is allowed.
Rule R-8: a booking must be SEATED before it can be COMPLETED.
CONFIRMED -> SEATED. The table flips to OCCUPIED.
Table status is kept in step with its bookings automatically.

item.name: DELETE - seated booking cannot be deleted (422)

request.description: A booking in progress must be completed first.
SEATED -> COMPLETED, a final state.
Rule R-9.

item.name: 4. Cross-entity rules and cleanup
item.description: Shows the delete guards between the three entities, then clears the test data.

item.name: CREATE - fresh booking for the delete tests (201)
DELETE - customer with an active booking (422)

request.description: BR-05 guard: history stays consistent, so the booking must be cancelled first.

item.name: DELETE - table with an active booking (422)

request.description: Same guard on the table side.

item.name: UPDATE - table out of service while booked (422)

request.description: A booked table cannot be taken out of service without stranding the guest.
Now that no active booking remains, the delete succeeds.
